Effective waste management is a key component of CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.’s commitment to environmental sustainability, workplace safety, and full regulatory compliance. The company has implemented structured and systematic waste management practices across all stages of its pharmaceutical intermediate and specialty chemical manufacturing operations, including raw material handling, reaction processes, blending, packaging, quality control, maintenance, and utility activities.

The waste management process at CTX Lifesciences focuses on the following core procedures:

1. Waste Stream Mapping– Identification and recording of all waste types generated across operations.
2. Waste Segregation at Source – Separation of biodegradable, recyclable, and hazardous waste at the point of generation.
3. Reduction of Total Waste Generation – Adoption of process efficiencies and material optimization to minimize waste.
4. Safe Storage, Handling, and Transportation of Waste – Ensuring secure containment and movement of waste materials to prevent leaks, spills, or cross-contamination.
5. Environmentally Sound Disposal Methods – Disposal of waste through authorized recyclers and government-approved facilities, in line with environmental regulations.

This SOP establishes a comprehensive and standardized waste management procedure at CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. It aims to ensure proper segregation, classification, storage, handling, transportation, and disposal of all waste streams, while emphasizing environmental sustainability, worker safety, and compliance with applicable Indian regulations, including guidelines issued by the Pollution Control Board and other relevant authorities.

body.text:
Procedure
Segregation at Source: All waste must be placed immediately into the correct color-coded bins at the point of generation. No waste shall be mixed at any stage of handling, storage, or transport.
Collection and Internal Transfer: Departmental staff or housekeeping personnel shall collect waste at scheduled intervals to avoid overflow, ensure cleanliness, and prevent cross-contamination.
Temporary Storage: Each waste category shall be transferred to its designated interim storage area. Hazardous waste must remain in sealed and clearly labelled containers as per regulatory requirements until collected by authorized vendors.
Documentation & Register Updating: All waste quantities, categories, and disposal details shall be recorded in the centralized Waste Stream Register. Department heads must verify weekly entries for accuracy.
Final Disposal: Waste shall be disposed of through authorized recyclers, municipal authorities, or hazardous-waste vendors as per the disposal method listed in the Waste Stream Mapping Table.
Monitoring: Supervisors and the EHS Officer shall routinely inspect segregation practices and provide refresher training to departments where non-compliance is observed.
Corrective Actions

Immediate Response: Any instance of mis-segregation or cross-contamination must be corrected immediately. Waste shall be re-segregated and handled according to the defined procedure.
Employee Retraining: Targeted training sessions are held for departments or shifts where errors are identified.
Root Cause Analysis: The EHS Officer shall investigate repeated non-compliance to identify process gaps and implement preventive measures.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): All staff involved in waste handling, especially hazardous and chemical waste, are equipped with appropriate PPE including gloves, safety goggles, masks, aprons, and closed footwear.
Spill Management: Trained personnel follow a documented Spill Response Protocol, using spill kits, absorbents, and neutralizing agents. All incidents are recorded in the spill log.

steps.heading: Promotion of Material Reuse and Recovery

body.text:
Identification of Recoverable Materials

A periodic waste stream audit is conducted to identify recyclable and recoverable materials generated during the product manufacturing process. These materials include, but are not limited to:

Process Residue Waste: Recoverable residues such as filter cake and intermediates generated during reaction, filtration, and blending processes, where feasible for reprocessing or recovery.
Recyclable Paper Waste: Clean cardboard, paper sheets, kraft paper, and cartons from packaging areas and offices.
Recyclable Plastic Waste: Plastic films, liners, HDPE bags, and wrappers from raw material receiving and packaging areas.
Reject / Off-Spec Product Waste: Off-spec batches or rejected materials segregated in the QC department and warehouse, assessed for potential reprocessing or recovery.
Collection and Segregation

Designated bins and collection points are strategically placed within production, processing, and packaging areas for recoverable materials.
Training sessions and awareness programs are conducted to ensure all staff understand the value of reuse and their role in achieving waste reduction goals.
All recoverable waste is logged in the centralized Waste Stream Register, with departmental responsibility assigned for handling, storage, and disposal.

Recovery and Reuse Processes

Recoverable materials are processed to maximize reuse and minimize disposal. The process ensures materials are repurposed internally or sent to certified recyclers, as applicable.

4.1. Storage Procedures

Hazardous Waste

Containers for Hazardous Waste

Hazardous waste is stored in leak-proof, sealed, and chemically compatible containers to prevent leaks and contamination. These containers are chosen based on the specific chemical properties of the waste to ensure maximum safety. All containers remain securely closed except during waste loading activities.

Labeling of Hazardous Waste Containers

To ensure safe storage, handling, and disposal of hazardous waste, CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. follows mandatory labelling procedures in line with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, issued by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and enforced by the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB).

Labelling Specifications

Material: Labels are made of chemical-resistant and weatherproof material, suited for high-temperature and humid chemical manufacturing environments.
Size: Minimum dimensions of 4 x 6 inches, visible from at least 2 meters.
Font & Contrast: Bold text in English; font size minimum 12-point for key information; high contrast colors (e.g., black on white or red) for clear readability.
Adhesion: Labels must be securely affixed to resist heat, moisture, and chemical exposure.
Placement: Affixed to the upper front portion of each container for easy visibility during inspection and handling.
Label Must Include: “Hazardous Waste” and relevant hazard symbol(s); waste category and physical state (liquid, sludge, etc.); date of generation; generator’s name and contact details (CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.); emergency response information or hazard classification code.

Information Included on the Label

Each hazardous waste container includes the following:

Waste Type
Waste Code
Date of Generation
Quantity
Signal Word: DANGER
Hazard Statement: Flammable liquid and vapor. Toxic if inhaled.
Handling Instructions: Keep tightly closed. Store away from heat and flame.
Generator Name: CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.
Contact Person: Environmental Manager
Contact Details: +91-1234567891| hr@ctxlifesciences.com

d. Inspection and Maintenance

Labels are reviewed and annual internal waste audits are conducted to ensure clarity and regulatory compliance.
Damaged or unreadable labels are immediately replaced.
Any unlabeled containers are promptly flagged and relabeled by trained personnel.

e. Designated Storage Areas for Hazardous Waste

Hazardous waste is stored in clearly marked, secure areas away from operational zones.
Access is restricted to trained personnel only.
The storage zone features impervious flooring, bunds, proper ventilation, and fire suppression systems.
Regular inspections are conducted for leaks or container damage, with spill kits and emergency plans in place.
Non-Hazardous Waste Storage

Containers: Non-hazardous waste is stored in standard, non-leaking containers. These containers are not required to meet the same stringent specifications as hazardous waste containers but must still be durable enough to withstand normal handling conditions.
Labeling: Non-hazardous waste is not required to have detailed hazard labels, containers are clearly labeled to indicate the waste type (e.g., packaging waste, office waste).
Storage Areas: Non-hazardous waste is stored in designated collection areas that are separate from hazardous waste storage zones. These areas should be kept clean and organized to avoid cross-contamination with hazardous or recyclable waste.
Spill Containment: Spill containment materials are available near storage areas to address any accidental spills promptly.
Recyclable Waste Storage

Containers: Recyclable waste (e.g., plastics, paper) are stored in separate bins marked clearly with the type of material.
Sorting: Recycling bins are sorted according to the type of material (e.g., separate bins for plastics, paper, metal, and glass) to facilitate easy and efficient recycling.
Storage Area: Recyclables are stored in areas that is dry, clean, and away from potential contamination sources. The area is well-organized to facilitate easy access and transportation to recycling facilities.
Organic Waste Storage

Containers: Organic waste, such as food scraps or biodegradable materials, are stored in compostable or biodegradable bags or bins.
Storage Conditions: Organic waste are kept in a cool, ventilated area to prevent odor buildup and promote efficient decomposition.
Separation: Organic waste is kept separate from non-hazardous and recyclable waste to avoid contamination.

4.2. Handling Procedures

Hazardous Waste Handling

PPE: Mandatory use of gloves, goggles, masks/respirators, and protective gear based on hazard level.
Training: Staff receive regular training on safe handling, segregation, and emergency protocols.
Spill Control: Secondary containment is used. Any spill is managed as per CTX Lifesciences spill response plan.
Non-Hazardous Waste Handling

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): While non-hazardous waste handling does not typically require specialized PPE, workers should wear gloves and other general protective equipment to prevent minor injuries.
Handling Instructions: Non-hazardous waste should be handled with care to avoid contamination with hazardous or recyclable materials. The waste should be placed directly into designated containers to ensure segregation is maintained.
Safety Considerations: The handling area for non-hazardous waste should be kept clean and organized to ensure safe handling and quick access to storage or disposal facilities.
Recyclable Waste Handling

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Employees should wear gloves and any other PPE deemed necessary to handle recyclables safely.
Sorting: Employees must follow proper sorting instructions to ensure that recyclable materials are separated by type (e.g., plastics, paper) and are not contaminated by non-recyclable or hazardous materials.
Handling Procedures: Recyclables should be handled carefully to prevent breakage and must be compacted if needed to reduce volume and prepare them for transportation.
Organic Waste Handling

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Employees handling organic waste should wear gloves and any other suitable PPE to avoid direct contact with potentially contaminated materials.
Proper Handling: Organic waste must be handled in a manner that minimizes odor and contamination. Any spillage of organic material should be promptly cleaned up to prevent pests or other health risks.

4.3. Transportation Procedures

CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. ensures that hazardous waste is transported with the highest standards of safety, compliance, and traceability. All activities are performed in accordance with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and the applicable State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) guidelines.

Hazardous Waste Transportation

Licensed Contractors

All hazardous waste is transported exclusively by CPCB authorized hazardous waste transport contractors.
Contractors are required to hold valid transport licenses, vehicle fitness certificates, and personnel training certifications as per Rule 19 of the 2016 Hazardous Waste Rules.
Service-level agreements ensure contractors adhere to both national and state-level environmental laws and submit documentation before each dispatch.
Container Sealing and Vehicle Safety

Pre-Dispatch Inspection: All hazardous waste containers undergo visual and physical inspection by the EHS Officer to ensure they are undamaged, leak-proof, and compliant with prescribed specifications.
Container Specifications: Constructed of HDPE or corrosion-resistant steel. Equipped with tamper-evident lids and secure locking systems. Labeled in accordance with Schedule II of the 2016 Rules, including waste category, generation date, and hazard symbols in English.
Transport Vehicle Safety Features: Equipped with spill containment trays, absorbent lining, and segregation compartments. Clearly marked with “HAZARDOUS WASTE” placards, including appropriate UN hazard codes and color-coded labels. Vehicle body inspected for container stability and tie-down security prior to dispatch.

Documentation and Regulatory Compliance

Each shipment is accompanied by a full set of documentation as required under Rule 19 of the Hazardous Waste Rules and SPCB SOPs:

Form 10 – Hazardous Waste Manifest: Contains generator details, transporter information, quantity, physical state, and final disposal location. Signed by the generator (CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.), transporter, and TSDF upon completion.
Transport Authorization Certificate: Verified copy of contractor’s waste transport approval issued by the SPCB.
Safety Data Sheets (SDS): Specific to the hazardous material being transported. Includes chemical composition, physical properties, hazards, first aid measures, and firefighting precautions.

Emergency Preparedness and Response

Transport vehicles are equipped and staffed to handle emergency situations involving hazardous waste.

On-Board Emergency Kit Includes: Absorbent pads, neutralizing agents, spill containment socks, waste collection bags; complete set of PPE: gloves, masks, aprons, goggles, face shields; fire extinguisher and first-aid kit.
Personnel Training: Drivers and accompanying staff are trained in classification and handling of hazardous waste under Indian rules; on-site spill containment, evacuation procedures, and safe zone establishment; immediate communication protocols with SPCB, local authorities, and emergency responders; first aid and hazard-specific response techniques.
Emergency Plan Adherence: Transport staff must follow CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.’ Emergency Response Plan (ERP) including rapid isolation of spill zone, notification to Environmental Compliance Officer and SPCB, and activation of third-party emergency cleanup services, if necessary.
Transportation Execution and Post-Delivery Verification

Route Planning and Pre-Dispatch Checks: Transported via pre-approved, low-risk routes identified to minimize environmental and human health risks. Vehicles undergo pre-departure inspections for container integrity, proper label display, documentation readiness, and secure cargo placement.
Segregation of Incompatibles: Flammable, reactive, or corrosive substances are stored separately within the transport vehicle, using CPCB-compliant segregation barriers.
Delivery and Reconciliation at TSDF: On reaching the authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facility (TSDF), waste is unloaded under supervision; quantity and type are verified against manifest entries; any discrepancies are documented, reported, and investigated. Form 10 is updated, signed, and one copy is returned to CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. for records.
Non-Hazardous Waste Transportation

Transportation Vehicles: Non-hazardous waste is transported using regular vehicles designed to carry bulk waste. These vehicles should be equipped with secure and leak-proof containers to prevent contamination during transit.
Route Planning: Non-hazardous waste should be transported directly to disposal or recycling facilities without unnecessary detours to minimize time and risk of spillage.
Recyclable Waste Transportation

Designated Vehicles: Recyclable materials should be transported in vehicles dedicated to recycling operations to ensure they are not contaminated by other waste streams.
Proper Sealing: Recyclable materials should be securely stored in containers to prevent leakage, breakage, or contamination during transportation.
Organic Waste Transportation

Transport Containers: Organic waste should be transported in sealed, vented containers to prevent odors and exposure to contaminants. Containers should be easy to unload at composting or organic recycling facilities.
Transportation Vehicles: Organic waste is transported using trucks or vehicles designed for organic waste, with a focus on maintaining a hygienic and controlled environment during transit.

Hazardous Waste Treatment and Disposal

CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. is committed to minimizing the environmental and human health impacts of hazardous substances generated during production through the implementation of specialized treatment protocols and safe disposal systems. These procedures are aligned with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) directives.

Specialized In-House Treatment Techniques

Hazardous waste generated during manufacturing is treated on-site using tailored methods, depending on its type and hazard level:

Neutralization Units: Used to treat acidic or alkaline wastewater and chemical residues, ensuring safe pH levels before storage or further processing.
Sludge Solidification: Sludge containing chemicals is stabilized using binding agents (like fly ash or lime) to convert it into a dry, non-leachable form suitable for secure landfilling.
Solvent Recovery and Segregation: High-value spent solvents are separated and stored for off-site recovery, reducing environmental load and enabling circular use.
Container Cleaning Units: Used chemical drums are triple-rinsed and stored safely for return to suppliers or scrap recovery vendors.
Contaminated PPE Handling: Soiled gloves, rags, and aprons are collected in labelled containers and prepared for co-processing or incineration.

All treatment processes are managed by trained EHS personnel with regular monitoring to ensure effectiveness and safety.

Safe and Compliant Disposal

After treatment, hazardous waste is dispatched to CPCB/SPCB-authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs):
Documentation and Monitoring

Form 10 (Manifest): Tracks each shipment from source to disposal
Disposal Certificates and SDS records are maintained for each waste category
Annual Form IV submitted to SPCB as per compliance norms
Monthly waste reconciliation conducted to verify treatment vs. disposal ratios

CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.’ integration of specialized treatment techniques with regulatory-compliant disposal helps reduce long-term environmental impacts and supports its broader commitment to responsible production and chemical safety.

Non-Hazardous Waste Disposal

Municipal or Approved Landfills: Non-hazardous waste, if not reused or recycled, is disposed of via local municipal waste systems or sent to government-approved landfills, in accordance with local environmental guidelines.
Recordkeeping: Disposal quantities and routes are recorded and retained to ensure traceability and compliance.
Organic Waste Disposal

Composting & Organic Processing Units: Organic waste is sent to authorized composting sites or organic recycling facilities where it is transformed into compost or energy-rich material. This supports soil health and reduces environmental burden.
Documentation: Disposal volumes and destinations are recorded to maintain transparency and support sustainability reporting.

steps.heading: Material Consumption Reduction by process optimization

body.text: Process Innovation for Precise Material Use
All chemicals, solvents, and process agents are dispensed using automated dosing systems to ensure accurate quantities based on batch requirements, preventing overuse or underuse of materials.

During synthesis, reaction, and purification processes, parameters such as temperature, pressure, time, and concentration are closely controlled through advanced monitoring systems to optimise material usage and minimise wastage.

Continuous monitoring of production data is conducted allowing the operators to make precise adjustments in formulations and process conditions in real time, maintaining consistent product quality while reducing excess consumption of chemicals and water.
Equipment and recycling systems are routinely inspected and maintained to ensure proper functioning, consistent output, and adherence to efficiency and sustainability standards.
Reintegration of Recovered Input Materials

Residual solvents, process water, and chemical residues from previous batches are systematically collected, treated, tested, and reused in subsequent processes wherever feasible, reducing dependency on fresh resources and supporting sustainability goals.
The collected residues are passed through filtration units to remove impurities and treated as per standard chemical recovery protocols to ensure quality and safety for reuse.
Treated materials undergo quality testing to verify concentration, composition, and suitability for reuse in non-critical production processes.
Approved recovered materials are reintroduced into subsequent production batches in controlled quantities to replace virgin raw materials.
All recovery and reuse activities are recorded in material usage logs, including batch details, recovered volume, and percentage of reuse.
The EHS and Production teams jointly review recovery performance monthly to ensure efficiency, cost savings, and compliance with sustainability objectives.
Enhanced Production Planning and Process Scheduling
Production batches are scheduled based on accurate demand forecasts and available machine capacity to ensure optimal utilization of resources and avoid overproduction or excess material use.
Scheduling is designed to reduce frequent machine changeovers, thereby minimizing the consumption of cleaning agents, solvents, purge materials, and water used between batches.

Similar product formulations, chemical compositions, and process-compatible batches are scheduled consecutively to minimise equipment cleaning, solvent flushing, and preparation requirements between production runs.
By aligning batch size with operational capacity, idle machine time and material wastage are minimized, improving overall production efficiency.
Production schedules are periodically reviewed and adjusted based on actual performance data and material consumption trends to enhance planning accuracy and sustain material efficiency.

steps.heading: Use of Eco-Friendly and Biodegradable Raw materials

body.text: CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. follows a focused strategy to minimize production waste and reduce environmental impact by integrating eco-friendly and biodegradable raw materials throughout its manufacturing operations. The following practices are implemented across all units:

Environmentally Responsible Raw Materials: CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. prioritises the use of high-purity raw materials and intermediates that generate minimal impurities and by-products, thereby reducing waste generation at the source.
Low-Toxicity Chemical Inputs: Process chemicals and reagents are selected based on lower toxicity profiles and controlled reactivity, minimising hazardous waste generation and environmental impact.
High-Efficiency Reaction Systems: Optimised reaction pathways and catalysts are used to achieve higher conversion rates, reducing unreacted residues and minimising process waste.

Water-Based and Safer Alternatives: Preference is given to water-based or less hazardous process alternatives where technically viable, reducing dependency on harmful solvents and lowering effluent treatment load.

Certified Inputs Only: All raw materials are procured in compliance with applicable regulatory standards (e.g., REACH, RoHS, and internal quality standards), ensuring environmental safety and responsible usage.

Vendor Qualification and Re-Assessment: Suppliers are approved only after documentation and samples verify the biodegradability and chemical safety of materials. Vendor compliance is re-evaluated every quarter to phase out materials that may have waste-intensive profiles.

steps.heading: Adoption of Safer alternative & less-hazardous Substances

substeps.text: Identification of Hazardous Inputs

A quarterly review of all chemicals used in synthesis, processing, purification, and cleaning operations is conducted to identify substances listed under applicable regulatory frameworks such as REACH (Annex XVII), BIS safety standards, and other relevant hazardous chemical lists.
Substitution with Greener Alternatives
Solvents & Cleaning Agents: Hazardous and high-VOC solvents are replaced, where feasible, with low-toxicity or water-based alternatives, ensuring safer handling and reduced environmental impact.
Process Chemicals: Conventional high-risk reagents are substituted with safer, less hazardous alternatives that offer similar efficiency while minimising waste generation and toxicity.
Oxidising / Reducing Agents: High-impact chemicals are replaced with more controlled and environmentally acceptable agents to reduce hazardous by-products and improve operator safety.
Catalysts & Reagents: Preference is given to high-efficiency catalysts that improve reaction yield and reduce unreacted residues and process waste.
Additives & Processing Aids: Wherever feasible, biodegradable or lower-impact additives are used to minimise environmental load and improve treatability of effluents.
Pre-Approval and Testing

All alternative chemicals undergo compatibility testing with process conditions and product requirements before approval. Only inputs with proven performance and compliance with applicable regulatory standards (e.g., REACH, internal quality standards) are permitted for production use. Production staff are trained during the implementation of each substitution.
Monitoring and Recordkeeping

Effluent discharge data, chemical consumption records, and supplier MSDS are reviewed monthly to ensure substituted inputs are in continuous use and meet environmental benchmarks. Audit trails are maintained for verification.

steps.heading: Reducing Hazardous By-Product Formation and Toxicity

body.text: CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. has implemented a series of proactive measures to limit the generation of hazardous by-products during production processes and reduce their impact on the environment:

Conventional high-impact solvents and reagents are replaced, where feasible, with low-toxicity or water-based alternatives, reducing emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and hazardous residues.
Process conditions such as temperature and pH are carefully controlled to prevent Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) formation.
Advanced filtration and chemical recovery systems are installed to capture and reclaim residual substances before they enter the effluent stream.
All hazardous wastes are treated and disposed of through government authorized facilities, ensuring full compliance with applicable national regulations.
Routine audits of chemical usage and waste management practices are carried out to ensure continued compliance and to identify opportunities for improvement.

This Efficient Energy Management SOP outlines CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.’s structured approach to optimizing energy consumption across all pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturing and processing operations. The strategy is aligned with national and international sustainability goals, incorporating energy-efficient machinery, renewable energy adoption, and waste heat recovery systems to reduce environmental impact.

Additional measures include fuel switching, smart monitoring technologies, and active employee participation to strengthen overall efficiency. This SOP supports CTX’ broader ESG objectives by ensuring continuous improvement, compliance with energy management standards, and measurable reductions in carbon emissions and operational costs.

To define a comprehensive energy management procedure that enhances operational efficiency, reduces environmental impact, and supports long-term sustainability across pharmaceutical intermediate and specialty chemical manufacturing processes.
This SOP is applicable to all sites, departments and equipment within CTX Lifesciences manufacturing facilities that consume energy during daily operations.
The following procedures reflects the established practices implemented to enhance energy efficiency, optimize resource utilization, and minimize environmental impact in our operations.

body.text: To enhance energy efficiency and reduce overall electricity consumption, CTX Lifesciences has implemented the following machine-level optimization strategies:

substeps.text: Upgrade to Energy-Efficient Equipment: CTX Lifesciences production units, including reactors, centrifuges, dryers, and material handling systems, are equipped with modern inverter-based motor drives that adjust speed and load according to process requirements. Variable frequency drives (VFDs) help machines run at optimal energy levels, reducing consumption during low-load conditions. Older, high-energy-consuming machineries are systematically replaced with BEE-rated or equivalent certified machinery to enhance energy efficiency. Energy efficiency within the steam distribution system is improved through the installation of steam traps. Steam traps automatically remove condensate and non-condensable gases while preventing live steam from being discharged into the condensate line, thereby ensuring efficient heat transfer and significantly reducing energy losses. The Air Handling Unit (AHU) systems operating with compressor-based cooling have been replaced with centralized cooling system comprising three 125 TR water chiller units to improve cooling efficiency and hence optimize overall energy utilization within the facility.

Process Automation Using PLCs: Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) are integrated into key production lines, such as reactors, filtration units, and drying equipment to regulate operations based on real-time process requirements. Machines automatically start, pause, or stop based on load sensors and production cycle triggers, reducing idle running and standby energy use. Sequential operations are interlocked so that subsequent processes only activate when previous stages are complete, ensuring precise control over runtime and energy consumption.

Energy Performance Monitoring and Preventive Maintenance: Critical equipment, including reactors, centrifuges, dryers, and utility systems, is connected to energy meters to provide continuous data on energy usage, efficiency, and anomalies. The engineering and EHS teams review this data weekly to identify inefficiencies or abnormal consumption patterns. Preventive maintenance schedules are guided by energy performance data to: Maintain optimal machine operation. Prevent overheating, mechanical wear, and inefficiency due to misalignment or aging parts. Extend the operational lifespan of machines, reducing the environmental footprint of equipment replacement.

body.text: CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. has upgraded its lighting infrastructure to reduce energy consumption while ensuring safe and well-illuminated workspaces across all operations.

substeps.text: LED Lighting Retrofit: All outdated fluorescent, incandescent, and halogen lighting systems have been replaced with energy-efficient LED fixtures in production areas, bag assembly sections, warehouses, and administrative offices. LEDs are selected for high lumen-per-watt efficiency and long lifespan, delivering maximum light output with minimal power consumption. This retrofit has led to measurable reductions in lighting-related energy usage and lower maintenance requirements.

Motion and Daylight Sensors: Motion sensors are installed in low-traffic areas such as storage rooms, corridors, and restrooms, ensuring lights are activated only when needed. Daylight sensors are installed near windows and skylights to automatically dim or switch off artificial lighting when sufficient natural light is available. Combined, these sensors prevent unnecessary energy use during non-operational hours and daylight periods.

Zonal and Smart Lighting Controls: The facility is divided into independent lighting zones based on activity areas and occupancy schedules. For example: Production and bag assembly zones operate on extended schedules. Storage, loading, and utility zones follow reduced lighting cycles. Smart control systems use programmable timers and real-time data to dynamically adjust lighting intensity and duration based on: Occupancy sensors, Time-of-day settings, Natural light availability. Emergency and exit lighting systems remain exempt from automated controls to ensure continuous safety compliance.

Automated Monitoring and Performance Tracking: The installed rooftop solar PV system is equipped with advanced monitoring software that continuously tracks: Real-time energy generation and cumulative output. System efficiency and panel performance trends. Deviations from expected parameters, such as voltage irregularities or sudden output drops. Alerts are automatically triggered in the event of system anomalies, enabling prompt diagnostics and corrective measures.

Preventive Maintenance and Inspection Schedule: Solar Panel Cleaning: Carried out at regular intervals (e.g., monthly), depending on local environmental conditions. This ensures removal of dust, dirt, bird droppings, or debris that can obstruct sunlight and reduce efficiency. Component Inspection: Routine inspections are conducted for: Inverters and Junction Boxes – checked for faults, overheating, or signs of internal wear. Cabling and Connectors – examined for physical damage, corrosion, or loose connections. Mounting Structures – assessed for structural integrity, rust, and anchoring stability.

Fault Response and Corrective Maintenance: Any deviations or underperformance identified by the monitoring system are immediately reported to the maintenance team. On-site diagnostics are carried out to identify issues such as: Malfunctioning inverters or failed modules. Faulty connectors, wiring damage, or panel shading. Identified faults are promptly addressed through repair or component replacement using certified parts, ensuring minimal system downtime.

Health, Safety, and Risk Control Measures: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): All personnel engaged in maintenance activities are required to wear appropriate PPE, including electrical-grade gloves, helmets, eye protection, non-conductive footwear, and harnesses for rooftop access. Lockout/Tagout (LOTO): Strict LOTO procedures are followed before performing maintenance to eliminate the risk of electrical shock or unintended activation. Fire Safety Compliance: Electrical installations are maintained in accordance with fire safety norms. Appropriate fire extinguishers (Class C-rated) are readily available near control panels and inverter stations.

Documentation, Recordkeeping, and Compliance: Comprehensive records are maintained covering: Daily, weekly, and monthly energy production data. Scheduled maintenance, cleaning logs, and fault resolutions. System performance trends and deviation reports. Regulatory Compliance: Operations align with the Electricity Act, 2003, CEA Safety Regulations, and relevant Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) for solar installations. Periodic internal audits are conducted to ensure continued compliance and system optimization.

steps.heading: Heat Recovery and Thermal Energy Optimization

body.text: To enhance energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions, CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. has implemented a waste heat recovery system within its chemical processing and utility operations.:

substeps.text: Heat Recovery from DG Set: The diesel generator (DG) set generates substantial heat from engine exhaust gases and the coolant system. This heat is captured using Exhaust gas heat exchangers. These exchangers extract thermal energy from the hot exhaust gases. The recovered thermal energy is then used for preheating process water and maintaining operational temperatures in production areas. Utilizing this recovered heat reduces reliance on external fuel-based heating systems, lowering energy consumption and cutting carbon emissions.

Thermal Insulation of Pipelines: All hot water and steam pipelines connected to DG set heat recovery systems are fitted with high-quality insulation to minimize thermal losses. Insulation helps maintain consistent process temperatures, shortens heating cycle times, and improves overall thermal efficiency.

Reduced Dependence on External Energy Sources: By reusing internally generated heat, the system reduces reliance on external heating systems such as electric boilers or fossil-fuel-based heaters. This results in: Lower energy consumption, Reduced fuel usage, A measurable decrease in carbon dioxide emissions. The initiative directly supports CTX Lifesciences sustainability and decarbonization goals, aligning with both internal targets and external environmental compliance frameworks.

steps.heading: Cleaner Fuel Transition and Emissions Control

substeps.text: Transition to Cleaner Fuel Sources: All operational diesel-fired boilers have been replaced with biomass-fired boilers, ensuring the use of cleaner, renewable fuel sources across production and processing areas. The biomass fuel consists of sustainable organic materials such as briquettes and agro-residues, which are routinely used to maintain consistent combustion efficiency and minimize environmental impact. Biomass-fired boilers are integrated into daily production schedules, providing stable and reliable heat for API manufacturing, chemical processing, and associated plant activities. Boiler operations follow optimized fuel usage protocols, which are consistently applied to maximize energy efficiency and maintain process reliability. Fuel consumption, emissions, and thermal efficiency are continuously monitored to ensure optimal boiler performance. Scheduled audits and routine maintenance are carried out to maintain consistent operation and prevent energy wastage. The use of biomass fuel has resulted in measurable reductions in CO₂, SO₂, and particulate matter emissions. Improved fuel efficiency contributes to reduced operating costs while sustaining production capacity. These practices support CTX Lifesciences’ ongoing decarbonization and sustainability initiatives.

Installation of Emission Monitoring Systems: All new combustion systems are equipped with continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) that provide real-time data on: Stack emissions (CO₂, NOₓ, SOₓ, and particulate matter), Combustion temperature and efficiency. These systems allow the engineering team to: Adjust air-to-fuel ratios dynamically for clean combustion, Detect abnormal pollutant levels early, Maintain compliance with national and state-level pollution control norms.

Performance Audits and Operational Oversight: Routine energy and emissions audits are carried out quarterly by the EHS and engineering teams to: Evaluate combustion performance, Identify maintenance needs, Recommend tuning or retrofitting where efficiency drops are observed. All findings are documented in boiler performance logs and used to update the facility’s energy management action plan.

steps.heading: Carbon Emissions Monitoring, Reduction, and Capture Procedure

body.text:
As part of its decarbonization and climate action strategy, CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. has implemented Amine-Based Post-Combustion Carbon Capture (PCC) Technology to reduce CO₂ emissions generated during pharmaceutical manufacturing and chemical processing operations.

In this system, process exhaust gases generated during chemical reactions, solvent recovery, and thermal operations are channelled through a carbon capture unit, where CO₂ is separated using an amine-based absorption system. The specific technology employed is: Amine-Based Post-Combustion Capture using Monoethanolamine (MEA) Solvent System

Once captured: The CO₂ is purified and compressed for safe geological storage or considered for industrial reuse where viable. The monoethanolamine (MEA) solvent is regenerated through a stripping process and recycled back into the system for continuous operation.

Key operational features include: Continuous performance monitoring to assess CO₂ capture efficiency, solvent degradation, and emission reductions. Scheduled preventive maintenance to ensure reliable operation and maximize energy efficiency. Detailed reporting on captured CO₂ volumes and energy consumption to support compliance with environmental regulations and internal sustainability targets.

By adopting this proven amine-based carbon capture technology, CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. strengthens its commitment to reducing its carbon footprint and integrating clean technologies into its core refining and recycling processes.

Carbon Footprint Calculation: CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. undertakes comprehensive carbon footprint assessments to quantify and manage its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The calculation process follows internationally recognized standards, primarily the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and global comparability. Emissions are systematically categorized into:

substeps.text: Scope 1 – Direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by the company, such as emissions from boilers, generators, and manufacturing equipment.
Scope 2 – Indirect emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity, steam, or other forms of imported energy used in production and administrative operations.

Scope 3 – Other indirect emissions that occur in the value chain, including emissions from upstream activities (e.g., raw material transportation, supplier emissions) and downstream activities (e.g., product distribution, waste disposal, and employee commuting).

To support this process, CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. maintains energy consumption data, production volumes, transport logs, and supplier information. These data points are used to calculate CO₂-equivalent emissions across all scopes. Regular third-party carbon audits are performed to monitor emissions trends over time, assess progress toward emission reduction targets, and identify opportunities for further energy efficiency or cleaner technologies. These audits also aid in maintaining regulatory compliance, improving environmental transparency, and guiding sustainability initiatives across operations. By embedding carbon footprint calculations into its environmental management system, CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. strengthens its strategic approach to sustainability and reaffirms its commitment to mitigating climate change.

substeps.text: Planning and Preparation: The energy audit is scheduled once in a three-year block, in coordination with an authorized third-party energy audit firm. Key energy systems and equipment at CTX Lifesciences, including reactors, distillation units, thermal fluid heaters, process heaters, heat economizers, expansion tanks, pump skids, conveyors, mixers, air compressors, chillers, pumps, motors, and lighting systems, are identified in advance for detailed evaluation to optimize energy efficiency and support the company’s sustainability initiatives. Details of equipment load, usage hours, operating efficiency, and power system layout are recorded across departments. Recommendation and Reporting: The audit findings are compiled into a detailed Energy Audit Report, which includes: Energy Conservation Measures (EnCon), Cost-benefit analysis, Estimated savings in kWh and ₹, Required investment and payback periods.

Implementation and Follow-up: All approved recommendations are scheduled for phased implementation. The plant team integrates energy-efficient solutions. The objective of this SOP is to establish a systematic approach for the efficient use, conservation, and management of water resources at CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. It aims to minimize water consumption, promote responsible usage across operations, and ensure proper monitoring and control of water-related activities within the facility.

This SOP applies to all water-related activities within CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.’s manufacturing and utility operations. It covers water usage in production processes, utilities, cleaning activities, and other supporting operations, along with monitoring and conservation measures implemented across the facility.

body.text:
The operations, maintenance, and EHS teams conduct routine inspections of the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and Multiple Effect Evaporator (MEE) units, including feed tanks, pumps, pipelines, valves, and storage tanks prior to operation.
Operators verify that chemical dosing systems, pH adjustment units, and treatment chemicals are available and functioning properly.
Safety personnel confirm the availability of personal protective equipment (PPE), spill containment materials, and emergency response equipment.

Influent Monitoring

Effluent generated from manufacturing and utility operations is collected and routed to the ETP for treatment.
Key parameters such as pH, temperature, TDS, COD, and flow rates are monitored regularly to ensure proper treatment performance.

Effluent Treatment

Wastewater generated from manufacturing and utility operations is treated through a multi-stage treatment process within the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP). These stages include primary treatment for removal of suspended solids, secondary biological treatment for degradation of organic matter, and tertiary treatment for further purification and polishing of the treated effluent.
During these treatment stages, residual Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), intermediates, and other pharmaceutical compounds present in the wastewater are reduced through chemical neutralization processes. These processes help break down complex pharmaceutical residues and minimize their presence in the treated water.
Electrolyte or coagulant chemical such as ferric chloride is added in controlled quantities in the neutralization tank, while air blowers ensure proper mixing and floc formation for effective removal of suspended contaminants.
After coagulation, a dedicated API removal step is implemented prior to final settling to reduce residual Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and pharmaceutical intermediates present in the effluent.
Advanced treatment methods such as activated carbon adsorption or chemical oxidation are applied where required to further reduce trace pharmaceutical compounds. The treatment method is selected based on periodic assessment of effluent characteristics and API load.
Treated effluent is regularly monitored for parameters such as pH, COD, TDS, and residual API levels to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory standards. Any deviation in treatment efficiency is reported to the EHS team, and corrective actions are implemented promptly.

Water Recovery and Reuse

Treated water suitable for reuse is stored in designated storage tanks and reused for non-critical applications such as floor cleaning, utility washing, cooling systems, and other auxiliary activities.
Concentrated residues from the MEE are handled and disposed of according to applicable environmental regulations and approved waste management procedures.

Sampling & Testing

Treated water is sampled periodically and analyzed for parameters such as pH, COD, TDS, and suspended solids to verify compliance with internal standards and regulatory limits.

Any deviation in treatment performance or water quality is immediately reported to the Environmental Compliance Officer (ECO) or designated responsible personnel.
Corrective actions may include adjusting chemical dosing, modifying operational parameters, conducting equipment maintenance, or increasing monitoring frequency.
All deviations and corrective actions are recorded and reviewed to ensure effective resolution.

Operators ensure that tanks, pumps, pipelines, and surrounding work areas are maintained in clean condition after operations.
Shutdown procedures for the ETP and MEE systems are carried out according to operational guidelines.
Daily records of operational parameters, water quality results, and maintenance activities are maintained.

In case of ETP or MEE system malfunction, overflow, or accidental spillage, operators initiate emergency shutdown and containment measures.
The EHS department is notified immediately, and corrective measures are implemented.
Incident details are documented, and preventive measures are reviewed to avoid recurrence.

Treated water recovered through the ETP and MEE systems is utilized for various non-potable applications within the facility to promote efficient water utilization and reduce dependence on freshwater sources.

Typical reuse applications include:

Cooling Systems: Treated water recovered from the ETP and MEE systems is utilized in cooling towers or condenser circulation systems to support heat exchange processes within manufacturing and utility operations. This helps maintain efficient cooling performance while reducing reliance on fresh water sources.
Equipment Cleaning: Recovered water is used for washing reactors, vessels, pipelines, and other processing equipment during routine cleaning activities. The use of treated water for these purposes ensures effective cleaning while optimizing water resource utilization.
Utility Applications: Treated water is supplied for general utility requirements such as washing of containers, maintenance activities, and other auxiliary operational needs within the facility.
Floor and Facility Cleaning: Recycled water is utilized for routine floor washing, housekeeping activities, and sanitation of operational areas to maintain workplace hygiene while minimizing freshwater consumption.

Recycled water is allocated based on operational requirements and quality suitability. Storage tanks, transfer pipelines, and valves are inspected regularly to ensure safe handling and prevent contamination. All reuse volumes are recorded in the Water Reuse Log Sheet, and any deviation in quality or supply is reported to the Utilities Supervisor for corrective action.

Water Usage Optimization

Water-Efficient Washing & Cleaning Practices:

All washing and cleaning tasks are performed in accordance with standardized work instructions designed to ensure effective cleaning with minimal water use. These instructions specify:

Required Water Volume: Predefined litres per task to prevent overconsumption.
Nozzle Type & Spray Pattern: Use of high-pressure, low-flow nozzles and controlled-spray systems for optimal coverage.
Cleaning Sequence: A structured top-to-bottom process, moving from cleaner to dirtier areas to avoid repeated washing.
Maximum Duration: Fixed time limits for each cleaning task to maintain consistency and prevent water wastage.

To support these practices, all equipment is maintained routinely to ensure accurate flow control, avoid leakages, and sustain efficiency. Cleaning schedules are designed to balance hygiene needs with water conservation, preventing redundant or unnecessary washing activities. Additionally, all pharmaceutical-grade cleaning and sanitising agents used in the facility are low-rinse formulations, enabling effective cleaning without the need for extra rinse cycles or additional water beyond the specified limits. Treated water recovered from the on-site water treatment system is reused for non-potable cleaning activities such as floor washing, equipment exterior cleaning, and housekeeping tasks. The quality of reused water is verified regularly as per internal water-recycling procedures.

Water-Efficient Cooling Systems:

A Closed Water Cooling System comprising chilled water and chilled brine circuits has been adopted at CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. to minimize water consumption and enhance operational efficiency. Traditional once-through cooling systems consume large volumes of freshwater and result in significant water losses, whereas the closed-loop system continuously recirculates the same cooling medium. The chilled water system circulates water in a closed loop between the chiller, heat exchangers, and process equipment, ensuring negligible water loss except for minor make-up requirements. The chilled brine system is employed in applications requiring sub-zero cooling, using a brine solution (water mixed with salt) in a closed cycle to prevent evaporation losses. Both systems contribute to reducing the facility’s freshwater footprint, while also lowering the need for chemical dosing, water treatment, and related infrastructure. Integration of treated effluent from the ETP as make-up water for cooling towers further enhances water reuse and aligns operations with Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) objectives. The systems are configured to operate efficiently under variable load conditions, ensuring consistent cooling performance with optimized resource use. Routine monitoring and preventive maintenance are carried out to ensure optimal performance in terms of cooling efficiency, energy consumption, and system reliability.

Monitoring, Review, and Continuous Improvement

Water consumption across all washing, cleaning, and manufacturing operations is tracked through calibrated flow meters and daily logbooks. Monthly reviews are conducted to:

Identify deviations in water usage
Assess performance of rinse-recovery systems
Highlight equipment or operational inefficiencies
Recommend corrective and preventive actions

Operator feedback, internal audits, and performance evaluations are used to continually refine water-efficient practices and further reduce dependency on freshwater resources.

Rain Water Harvesting

To reduce dependency on groundwater and promote sustainable water use practices in line with government regulations, CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. has implemented a robust rainwater harvesting system integrated into its facility infrastructure.

Strategic Rooftop Collection:
Rainwater is collected from the extensive rooftop surfaces of production blocks, utility areas, and administrative buildings. These rooftops have been structurally designed or modified to ensure optimal water flow towards dedicated collection points without interference from exhaust outlets.
First-Flush Diverter Mechanism:
To ensure clean water collection, the first 2–3 mm of rainfall, which may contain dust, bird droppings, and other rooftop contaminants, is automatically diverted through a first-flush diverter system. This mechanism protects the storage tanks from initial impurities, ensuring better water quality for reuse.
Storage and Filtration Infrastructure:
Post-diversion, the cleaner rainwater is routed through gravel and sand-based filtration units and stored in underground RCC tanks built with protective coatings to prevent leaching or microbial growth. These tanks are fitted with level indicators, overflow protection, and maintenance access points.
Applications of Harvested Rainwater:
The stored rainwater is used for various non-potable industrial and facility-related purposes, including:
Cooling Tower Make-Up Water: Reduces demand on treated fresh water by supplementing cooling needs during high-load operations.
Toilet Flushing in Administrative and Production Areas: Helps save large volumes of water used in sanitary operations.
Landscape Irrigation: Ensures greener premises and cleaner surroundings without using borewell water.
Monitoring and Maintenance:
Water quality is periodically monitored for basic parameters such as pH, turbidity, and microbial content, especially for water directed to equipment like cooling towers. The tanks and filters are cleaned as per a bi-monthly maintenance schedule to prevent contamination and ensure system efficiency.

Groundwater Contamination Prevention

As part of its environmental risk management and regulatory compliance framework, CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD. has established structured groundwater and soil protection measures within its pharmaceutical manufacturing and chemical handling operations.

Engineered Containment Systems: RCC flooring with chemical-resistant coating and designated collection pits have been constructed in tant coatings and designated collection pits are provided in solvent storage, reaction, and handling areas. These engineered containment systems ensure that any accidental spills or leakages remain confined within a controlled boundary, preventing percolation into the soil and safeguarding underlying groundwater resources.
Safe Chemical Storage Practices: Process chemicals, including solvents, intermediates, and reagents are stored in sealed, corrosion-resistant drums and tanks that are clearly labelled and positioned within designated storage zones equipped with secondary containment arrangements. This controlled storage practice significantly minimises the possibility of uncontrolled discharge and environmental contamination.
Employee Training & Awareness: Periodic training sessions are conducted to ensure employees understand safe chemical handling, transfer procedures, spill prevention methods, and wastewater management practices. These awareness programs strengthen operational discipline and reduce the risk of groundwater contamination incidents.
Inspection & Preventive Maintenance: Hazardous material storage areas, pipelines, and transfer systems are routinely inspected and maintained to preserve containment integrity. Operational protocols include monitoring of storage conditions, scheduled leak detection checks, and immediate implementation of corrective measures in the event of any irregularities.
Documentation & Compliance Monitoring: Detailed documentation and systematic record-keeping are maintained for chemical inventories, inspection reports, maintenance logs, and employee training activities. This structured compliance framework supports adherence to environmental regulations and promotes continuous improvement in contamination prevention and environmental protection performance.

blocks.text: The Air Management Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines the steps taken to ensure effective control, monitoring, and reduction of air emissions in manufacturing processes. The primary focus is to minimize the impact of air pollutants such as particulate matter, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and gases, in line with regulatory standards. The SOP includes the use of air filtration systems, regular emissions monitoring, maintenance protocols for air handling equipment, and corrective measures for any non-compliance. These actions contribute to maintaining a healthy work environment and reducing the company’s overall environmental footprint.

To implement effective strategies and measures to prevent emissions of atmospheric pollutants and other environmental impacts in pharmaceutical intermediate and specialty chemical manufacturing operations.
The scope includes the implementation of measures to control and reduce atmospheric pollutants and other environmental impacts associated with production processes. This includes:

Installation of air filtration systems, to capture particulate matter.
Utilization of enclosed systems to reduce emissions.
Adoption of noise-dampening equipment in high-noise machinery areas and vibration isolation techniques.
Application of odor-neutralizing agents and ensuring proper ventilation in areas with volatile chemicals.

body.text: Particulate Matter Mitigation

High-efficiency dust collection systems are installed across material handling, powder processing, and packaging areas to control airborne particulate matter (PM) generated during manufacturing operations. These systems use bag filters with pulse-jet cleaning mechanisms that automatically remove accumulated dust and maintain consistent airflow and filtration efficiency.

Localized extraction systems are installed at material transfer and powder handling points to capture dust at the source. The collected dust is stored in sealed containers to prevent re-entrainment and is periodically transferred to authorized waste management facilities for safe disposal.

In addition, HEPA (High-Efficiency Particulate Air) filters are installed in air handling units and controlled processing areas to capture fine particulate matter and maintain indoor air quality. Continuous monitoring of pressure differentials and airflow, along with routine inspections and preventive maintenance, ensures efficient operation of the filtration systems.
Gaseous Emission Mitigation

Wet scrubbers are installed at process vents and boiler exhaust systems to capture and neutralize sulfur dioxide (SO₂), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and other acid gases generated during fuel combustion and chemical processing operations. Exhaust gases pass through an alkaline scrubbing solution where acidic components react to form neutral salts, ensuring emissions comply with regulatory standards.

Boiler exhaust systems are also equipped with closed-circuit gas recirculation (CCGR) units, which redirect a portion of flue gases back into the combustion chamber. This stabilizes combustion temperatures, reduces peak flame temperatures, and minimizes the formation of sulfur oxides (SOx) and nitrogen oxides (NOx). Automated controls and routine maintenance ensure efficient operation.
Fugitive Emission Mitigation

Fugitive emissions from reactors, pipelines, storage tanks, and material handling activities are controlled through enclosed systems, localized extraction units, and properly designed ventilation systems.

Air handling units equipped with HEPA filtration capture fine airborne contaminants and help prevent uncontrolled dispersion of particulates and odorous substances. Regular inspection and preventive maintenance of ventilation systems, ducts, valves, and filtration units ensure continuous performance and help maintain workplace air quality while minimizing environmental impact.
Monitoring and Maintenance:

Emission control systems are inspected monthly to ensure effective operation.
Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (CEMS) are in place at emission sources to monitor parameters such as SO₂, NOx, CO, and particulate matter.
Quarterly air sampling is performed by an accredited third-party laboratory.

blocks.text: The following emergency equipment is already installed and routinely maintained at CTX LIFESCIENCES PVT. LTD.:

Fire Safety Equipment: ABC and CO₂ fire extinguishers, fire hydrants with hose reels in high-risk zones, fire alarms, smoke detectors, fire blankets, and sand buckets.
First Aid and Medical Response: Fully stocked first aid kits in all departments (checked monthly), eye wash stations and emergency showers in chemical zones, and trained first aiders on each shift.
Spill Control and Containment: Chemical spill kits near storage/handling areas and secondary containment for hazardous substances.
Evacuation & Rescue Equipment: Emergency torches, clearly marked exits with emergency lighting, and a functional PA system tested during drills.

body.text:
Emergency equipment is deployed following thorough location-specific risk assessments conducted by the HSE Department in coordination with departmental heads.
Equipment placement considers: Nature of activity (e.g., chemical processing, storage, handling operations); Density of personnel; Proximity to potential hazards (fire, chemicals, machinery).
Fire extinguishers, spill kits, first aid boxes, and emergency lighting are mounted at eye level, within easy reach, and clearly labelled with glow-in-the-dark signage.
Each floor and department maintains an Emergency Equipment Layout Map, which is: Displayed at prominent locations such as entrance corridors and evacuation points; Updated annually or after any layout/operational changes.
A centralized Emergency Equipment Register is maintained by the HSE team, capturing location, equipment ID, type, and inspection due dates.

A monthly inspection schedule is implemented by the HSE Officer, and the inspection checklist includes: Physical condition (corrosion, leakage, damage); Expiry dates (first aid items, fire extinguishers, spill absorbents); Visibility and accessibility (not blocked or relocated); Tagging of inspection date and initials.
Fire extinguishers undergo: Monthly visual inspections; Annual servicing and pressure testing by a licensed vendor; Replacement if pressure gauge is below standard range or any damage is noted.
Eye wash stations and emergency showers are flow-tested weekly to ensure functionality and cleanliness.
A preventive maintenance log is reviewed quarterly to plan upcoming servicing and replacements proactively.
Inspection findings are documented in Form CTX/EHS/001 and deviations are flagged for immediate corrective action.

First aid kits are restocked every month by the EHS representative using a standardized checklist that includes sterile gauze, bandages, antiseptic cream, eye drops, burn ointments, painkillers, and gloves.
Used or expired items are replaced immediately.
Each kit includes a restocking card that logs previous usage and refill date.
Spill kits are replenished after any usage or at minimum on a quarterly basis. Contents include chemical absorbents, neutralizers, PPE (gloves, goggles), and disposal bags.
Emergency torches and batteries are checked and replaced semi-annually or sooner if found non-functional during drills.
All damaged or expired equipment is marked with “DO NOT USE” tape and immediately removed from the active area.
Disposal of such items, especially chemicals and medical supplies, is carried out as per Hazardous Waste Management Rules and documented with vendor disposal slips.

All new employees receive mandatory training during induction on: Location and use of fire extinguishers, eye wash stations, and first aid kits; Emergency evacuation procedures and emergency contact points.
Refresher training sessions are held every 6 months and include: Live demonstrations by certified trainers; Department-wise hands-on practice for operating fire extinguishers and spill kits.
Mock evacuation drills are conducted annually in coordination with local fire and emergency services.
Drills are unannounced to simulate real scenarios. Includes timed evacuation, equipment use, and headcounts at designated assembly points.
Drill outcomes and training participation are recorded and reviewed during the HSE committee meetings for continuous improvement.

Do not tamper with machine guards.
Keep work areas clean and obstruction-free, especially in packing and storage zones.
Report unsafe conditions, near-misses, and spills immediately.

Smoking, running in the warehouse, and misuse of equipment are strictly prohibited.

Hand Protection: Cut-resistant or general-purpose gloves during material handling and packing.
Foot Protection: Safety shoes mandatory.
Eye Protection: Safety glasses where dust or flying particles may occur (inspection, unpacking).
Body Protection: High-visibility jackets in loading zones and during vehicle movement.

Only trained and authorised personnel may operate material-handling equipment such as pallet jacks, hand trolleys, forklifts, or drum lifters used for raw materials, intermediate products, and finished materials.
Conduct pre-use safety checks for equipment such as brakes, wheels, handles, safety locks, and alarms (where applicable).
Do not exceed load capacities when stacking raw materials, intermediate products, or finished goods on pallets, racks, or trolleys.
Use proper lifting techniques—bend knees, keep back straight, and hold loads close to the body—to prevent strain when handling heavy materials, drums, or cartons.
Utilise mechanical aids for heavy consignments or bulk loads to avoid manual overexertion and ensure operator safety.

Store raw materials, intermediates, and finished products in clearly labelled shelving systems or designated bin locations.
Keep different product types segregated (e.g., powders, liquids, packaged goods, accessories) to prevent mix-ups or cross-contamination.
Handle heavy drums, bulk containers, and large consignments with care, ensuring a secure grip to avoid hand injuries.
Ensure racks, shelves, and storage areas are not overfilled to prevent collapse or spillage of stored items.
Maintain dry, well-ventilated storage conditions to protect materials from moisture, contamination, or degradation.

Keep packing tables clean, organised, and free from loose materials, debris, or packaging scraps.
Use ergonomic workstations and anti-fatigue mats for prolonged handling of products, including bottles, drums, cartons, and accessory sets.
Dispose of packaging waste—such as cardboard, plastic liners, and other scrap materials—only in designated collection bins.
Avoid excessive force when sealing containers, tying bundles, or strapping packages to prevent strain or musculoskeletal injuries.
Ensure accurate labelling and barcoding of each product type before dispatch, including batch numbers, product codes, and handling instructions.

Do not use damaged electrical cords, plugs, extension boards, or portable equipment used in packing/dispatch areas.
Switch off all operational equipment—including mixers, reactors, pumps, filling machines, and weighing/dispensing units—when not in use.
Report any sparking, burning smell, overheating, or abnormal noise immediately to the Safety Officer.
Keep all electrical panels unobstructed and ensure dry surroundings, especially in storage zones where flammable chemicals or materials are present.

Ensure delivery trucks, vans, and cargo vehicles are completely stationary and secured before loading materials, drums, or packaged products.
Never stand beneath suspended loads during handling of bulk containers, pallets, or heavy consignments.
Use wheel stoppers, chocks, and dock levelers where required.
Maintain a safe distance from moving vehicles, forklifts, or trolleys in dispatch areas.
Ensure cartons, drums, or pallets of materials and finished products are stacked evenly and secured properly to avoid tipping or shifting during transport.

Ensure safe handling, dispensing, and storage of chemicals used in production, processing, cleaning, or adhesive/finishing operations.
Maintain up-to-date Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) for all chemicals at easily accessible locations.
Provide chemical-specific PPE such as chemical-resistant gloves, safety goggles, aprons, and face masks whenever handling solvents, reagents, cleaning agents, or other process chemicals.
Ensure proper ventilation or local exhaust systems in areas where vapours, fumes, or solvent-based inks are used.
Label all chemical containers clearly; never store chemicals in unmarked bottles or food containers.
Store chemicals in designated, well-ventilated storage areas away from heat, ignition sources, and pharma materials.
Follow the trainings provided on safe chemical handling, spill response, and emergency procedures.
Use spill kits immediately in case of chemical leaks; isolate the area and report to the supervisor.
Strictly prohibit eating, drinking, or smoking in areas where chemicals are stored or used.

Keep floors dry at all times; immediately clean water, oil, chemical, or solvent spills to prevent slips, especially in areas with powders, or liquid residues.
Use anti-slip mats in high-traffic zones such as packing, dispatch, and storage walkways.
Ensure adequate lighting in storage rooms, inspection areas, stairways, loading bays, and corridors.
Use handrails when ascending/descending stairs or ramps.
Secure loose cables, ropes, straps, and packaging materials away from pathways.
Do not climb on pallets, drums, storage racks, or unstable stacks.
Use certified ladders or platforms for stacking/unstaking high rack items; ensure stability before use.
Wear slip-resistant safety shoes in all operational zones.

Immediately clean spills of chemicals, powders, residues, and packaging waste to prevent slip, contamination, and fire hazards in all operational areas.
Keep emergency exits, fire extinguishers, and aisles clear at all times.
Maintain cleanliness in resting and eating areas; wash hands before breaks to avoid exposure to chemical residues, dust, or particulates.
Dispose of chemical, packaging, and process waste only in designated collection bins or containers, following CTX’s hazardous and non-hazardous waste management protocols to ensure environmental compliance and safety.

Inform supervisors immediately if feeling unwell, exhausted, or experiencing difficulty due to dust exposure.
Take scheduled rest breaks to reduce fatigue during repetitive packing or material-handling tasks.
Stay hydrated, especially during high-activity periods or hot weather.
Use appropriate PPE such as dust masks, respirators, or chemical-rated masks when handling powders, fine particulates, or chemical materials to prevent inhalation hazards.

Ensure workstations in chemical preparation areas, lab benches, inspection tables, weighing stations, and packing areas are adjusted to appropriate working height.
Maintain neutral posture: straight spine, relaxed shoulders, wrists aligned with forearms.
Use chairs with lumbar support and footrests where seated tasks are required for longer periods. (sampling, weighing, labelling, or quality inspections).

Rotate employees between tasks such as weighing, mixing, inspection, labelling, and packaging to reduce continuous strain.
Take micro-breaks every 30–60 minutes to stretch shoulders, wrists, fingers, and back.
Encourage short walking breaks for employees performing prolonged standing or sitting tasks.

Use ergonomic hand tools, pipettes, scoops, dispensers, and cutters with cushioned grips to minimise strain.
Keep tools within easy reach to avoid overextension.
Use magnifying tools and proper lighting for detailed inspections, labelling, or sampling.

Avoid excessive force when handling heavy chemical containers, bulk powders, or packaged intermediates.
Keep wrists straight and avoid prolonged twisting while performing repetitive packing movements.
